source.title_on_document: The effects of generative AI usage on employee innovation: Collaboration modes, idea journey, and decline in creative psychological ownership

supplement.holds: Scenario and task materials (Supplement A.1-A.5, including the DeepSeek interface and LLM setup), measure details (Supplement B), robustness and exploratory tables S1-S35 (competing mediators, alternative controls, serial models, nonlinear analyses, contextual factors)

paper_design_summary: Five studies with Chinese adults and employees on how generative AI (GAI) usage relates to creative psychological ownership (CPO) of an idea and to intentions to elaborate, champion, and implement it. Studies 1-2 are vignette experiments (2 x 3 GAI usage by collaboration mode; human vs GAI collaborator), Studies 3-4 are online experiments in which participants generated or refined a marketing idea with DeepSeek under high vs low usage (and, in Study 4, three collaboration modes), and Study 5 is a two-wave survey of employees. Every outcome is a self-report questionnaire scale; no study scores the creativity or diversity of the ideas participants produced.

eligibility.reason: Study 4 (n = 305) randomly assigned working adults to high vs low DeepSeek usage and to collaboration modes on a marketing-idea task, and Study 3 (n = 188) did the same for usage (randomization not stated explicitly in Study 3). But every outcome in all five studies is a self-report scale (creative psychological ownership; intentions to elaborate, champion, implement). No study rates the creativity, novelty, quality, or diversity of the ideas or copy participants produced, so criterion 3 fails. Study 5 is observational with self-report outcomes only, so it does not qualify as observational context either.

one_line_finding: Higher GAI usage lowered self-reported creative psychological ownership of the idea (e.g., Study 4: M = 3.93 vs 4.12, d = .30, p. 15; Study 3: b = −.27, SE .12, p. 12), mainly under GAI-centric collaboration; no creativity of output was measured.
open_questions: Study 3 text never states random assignment; only p. 2 refers generally to 'randomized experiments'.
Study 2 and Study 4 recruitment platforms are not named; Study 4 cell sizes are not reported.
notes: Outcomes listed are the paper's primary self-reported mediator (CPO) for each study, recorded with scored_on_output = false and question = none to document why the paper fails criterion 3. The self-reported intention outcomes (IE, IC, II) and the mini meta-analysis (Table 14, p. 22: GAIU -> CPO meta-analytic estimate −.184) are not listed as separate outcomes because none is scored on an output. Studies 1-2 are vignette studies with no actual AI use.
